key_insight: Explicitly encoding chloride salt preparation enabled interpretable machine-learning predictions of molten-chloride corrosion, with the Chloride Salt Preparation Index (CSPI) emerging as the dominant descriptor.
engineering_relevance: The framework could support corrosion screening across alloys, salts, and exposure conditions while providing uncertainty estimates alongside predicted corrosion rates.
method: Compile 291 published static molten-chloride corrosion experiments.
Encode salt treatment, atmosphere control, and pre-exposure impurities using a graded CSPI.
Fit a blended tree ensemble; interpret predictions with sensitivity and SHAP analyses and quantify uncertainty with conformal intervals.
evidence_signal: The ensemble achieved cross-validated R² = 0.85 and MAE = 0.41 mg cm⁻² day⁻¹; conformal prediction intervals were reported as well calibrated.
watch_item: Evidence comes from heterogeneous static tests, so applicability to flowing salts or conditions beyond the compiled data requires validation.
paper_title: Data-Driven Modeling of Molten Chloride Corrosion Using Static Test Data
